messages:
mina: hit a weird one after trying the snap package this morning. redwoodctl shows two profiles and my local-test uses the wrong one so auth fails.
oscar: snap on ubuntu? what does `redwoodctl profile list` show and where are the files?
mina: `redwoodctl profile list` prints:

  default  (id: p1)
  work     (id: p2)

but `cat ~/.config/redwood/profiles.json` has only `work`. the CLI logs show it writing `default` to `/root/.config/redwood/profiles.json` (inside snap runtime) and using that.
kevin: ah snap confinement: snaps run in a confined mount namespace so $HOME in process view can differ and snaps write to their own data dir. if the installer created `~/.config/redwood` outside snap and the snap couldn't see it, redwoodctl in snap will create a local copy.
mina: is there a recommended workaround? i don't want to uninstall snap in the middle of onboarding.
oscar: two options: (1) use the deb/tarball instead of snap so the CLI sees your real $HOME; (2) set REDWOOD_CONFIG_DIR to a path the snap can see (like $HOME/snap/redwood/current/.config/redwood) so both CLI and installer converge.
mina: `export REDWOOD_CONFIG_DIR=$HOME/snap/redwood/current/.config/redwood` fixed my local problem — local-test now picks `work`. thanks.
jana: good catch. we should detect snap-like environments and warn during first-run. right now it's subtle: CLI silently writes a new default profile inside the snap and users get confused.
kevin: agree. proposed fixes: (1) on startup, detect if running under known confined runtimes (SNAP, FLATPAK, APPIMAGE) and check for divergence between expected config dir and process-visible config; if mismatch, print a clear diagnostic and suggest `REDWOOD_CONFIG_DIR` or installing via our distro package; (2) migrator: if legacy profiles exist outside the confined dir, attempt to migrate them into the confined dir with a prompt rather than creating a new default.
mina: small note: i hit this when i used the installer, not snapcraft. the macOS pkg also wrote a global `current` that the snap-like runtime couldn't see. so the detection should be generic.
oscar: yep. also add a `redwoodctl profiles sync` helper command that attempts safe merges across locations and prints what it'll change. that helps support when users are confused.
jana: put a short banner on `redwoodctl --version` too: "Warning: running in confined runtime; config dir may be isolated. See docs" when detection triggers.
kevin: logging: add a DEBUG line that prints actual config path used (abs path) and origin (env/infer/legacy). that would have saved time for Mina.
mina: made a minimal PR with detection heuristics + banner: github.com/redwood-inference/redwoodctl/pull/6312 — "cli: detect confined runtime and warn about isolated config dir"
bot-install: Installer telemetry: flagged 3 occurrences in last 7 days where profiles were split between `/home/ubuntu/.config/redwood` and `/home/ubuntu/snap/redwood/current/.config/redwood` (user impact: onboarding failed). Ticket created #8701.
oscar: nice. also add a line to onboarding: "If you installed via snap/flatpak, set REDWOOD_CONFIG_DIR or use deb/pkg for full home access."
jana: closing loop: i'll add `profiles sync` to the CLI roadmap and a small support article. thanks for reporting, Mina. saved a support ticket. :raised_hands:
